# Data import and preparation

## Shared plotting constants

To keep figures visually consistent we fix the treatment colour palette once.

```{r plot-constants}
# Treatment colours used throughout (Pref = preference-based, EV = optimisation)
col_pref <- "#4E79A7"
col_ev   <- "#D55E00"
algo_cols <- c("Pref" = col_pref, "EV" = col_ev)
```

## Load raw data

Paths are relative to this script's location (replication-package layout).

```{r load-data}
choices <- read.delim("260206_1528_537_lotteryChoices.xls")
subjects <- read.csv("allSubjects.csv", header = TRUE)
prolificData <- read.csv("prolific_demographic_export_approved.csv")

choicesP1 <- subset(choices, Part == 1)
```

## Preregistered exclusions

We apply the preregistered exclusion rules: failed bot/slider check at first
attempt, failed comprehension checks after the second attempt, failure to
confirm careful participation (`Reliable < 6`), disclosed AI usage, incomplete
data (`Delegated < 0`), and the log-time "too fast" rule.

```{r exclusions}
# "Too fast" flag based on the preregistered log-completion-time rule
prolificData$logCompleTime <- log(prolificData$Time.taken)
prolificData$tooFast <- 1 * (
  prolificData$logCompleTime <
    mean(log(prolificData$Time.taken)) - 2 * sd(log(prolificData$Time.taken))
)

keep_ids <- prolificData$Participant.id[prolificData$tooFast == 0]

choices <- subset(
  choices,
  BotCheck1attempt == 1 &
    Part1CQsPassedOnAttempt <= 2 &
    Part2CQsPassedOnAttempt <= 2 &
    Reliable >= 6 &
    AIUsageInStudy == 0 &
    Delegated >= 0 &
    ProlificID %in% keep_ids
)

subjects  <- subset(subjects,  ProlificID %in% choices$ProlificID)
choicesP1 <- subset(choicesP1, ProlificID %in% choices$ProlificID)

# Final analysis sample (paper: N = 233; EV = 118, Pref = 115)
cat("Final sample size per condition (1 = EV, 0 = Preference-based):\n")
table(subjects$EVAlgorithm)

# Convenience label for the algorithm condition
choices <- choices %>%
  mutate(Algorithm = ifelse(EVAlgorithm == 1, "EV", "Pref"))
```

## Build participant-level Part-1 preference measures

These variables (revealed risk preferences from Part 1, per-task confidence,
and post-task expectations) are merged onto the decision-level `choices` data
for use in the regressions and the appendix coefficient plot.

```{r part1-measures}
# EV-maximising choice in each Part-1 task
choicesP1 <- choicesP1 %>%
  mutate(EVChoice = case_when(
    grepl("^P", ChoiceType) & PBetChosen == 1 ~ 1,
    grepl("^D", ChoiceType) & PBetChosen == 0 ~ 1,
    TRUE ~ 0
  ))

# "True" P-bet choice (less-risky choice when it was NOT EV-maximising)
choicesP1 <- choicesP1 %>%
  mutate(truePChoice = case_when(
    grepl("^D", ChoiceType) & PBetChosen == 1 ~ 1,
    TRUE ~ 0
  ))

# Participant-level Part-1 summaries
p1_summaries <- choicesP1 %>%
  group_by(ProlificID) %>%
  summarise(
    EVChoices    = sum(EVChoice),
    truePChoices = sum(truePChoice),
    PBet_count   = sum(PBetChosen),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

choices <- choices %>%
  left_join(p1_summaries, by = "ProlificID") %>%
  # per-task Part-1 confidence (matched on participant x option set)
  left_join(
    choicesP1 %>% select(ProlificID, OptionsetID, ConfidenceP1 = Confidence),
    by = c("ProlificID", "OptionsetID")
  ) %>%
  # participant-level demographics and post-task expectations
  left_join(
    subjects %>% select(
      ProlificID, Female, Age, Education, HHIncome,
      ProbOfBadComputerChoices, ProbOfAbsurdComputerChoices, ComputerRiskTaking
    ),
    by = "ProlificID"
  )
```

# Descriptive overview

## Choice quality and payoffs

Choice quality among non-delegated decisions and the payoff advantage of
delegation (paper, Section "Primary test: first-contact delegation").

```{r descriptives-choicequality}
# Share of non-dominated self-chosen options, by condition
choices %>%
  filter(Part == 2) %>%
  group_by(Algorithm) %>%
  summarise(
    avNonDom = mean(Nondominated[Delegated == 0 & Option > 0], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Average payoff: delegated vs. non-delegated decisions
# (paper: 243.49 points delegated vs. 195.18 points non-delegated, ~25% higher)
choices %>%
  filter(Part == 2) %>%
  group_by(Delegated) %>%
  summarise(meanPayoff = mean(RelevantPayoff, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

## Round-level delegation profile

```{r round-level-table}
choicesAv <- choices %>%
  filter(Part == 2) %>%
  group_by(Algorithm, WithinPartDecisionNumber) %>%
  summarise(
    avDeleg  = mean(Delegated, na.rm = TRUE),
    avNonDom = mean(Nondominated[Delegated == 0 & Option > 0], na.rm = TRUE),
    delegSE = sd(Delegated, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
choicesAv
```

## Figure 1 --- Average delegation over decisions

```{r figure1-average-delegation, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5}
fig1 <- choicesAv %>%
  mutate(Algorithm = factor(Algorithm, levels = c("EV", "Pref"),
                            labels = c("EV", "Preference-based"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = WithinPartDecisionNumber, y = avDeleg,

fig1
ggsave("Figure1_AverageDelegation.pdf", fig1, width = 7, height = 4.5)
```

# Primary test 1 --- First-contact delegation (round 1)

Preregistered one-sided Boschloo exact test on round-1 delegation
(paper: 66.9% vs. 55.8%, p = 0.041).

```{r boschloo-round1}
tab <- table(
  Delegated   = choices$Delegated[choices$Part == 2 & choices$WithinPartDecisionNumber == 1],
  EVAlgorithm = choices$EVAlgorithm[choices$Part == 2 & choices$WithinPartDecisionNumber == 1]
)

# Delegation share by condition (column 2 = EV)
prop.table(tab, margin = 2)

# One-sided Boschloo exact test (H1: EV > Pref)
exact.test(tab, method = "Boschloo", alternative = "greater", to.plot = FALSE)$p.value
```

## Effect size and CI for the round-1 contrast

Risk difference (Wald 95% CI) and odds ratio (Fisher's exact two-sided 95% CI), as
reported in the manuscript's new Table 1 (RD = 11.1pp [-1.3, 23.7]; OR = 1.60 [0.91, 2.84]).

```{r boschloo-round1-effectsize}
p_ev   <- prop.table(tab, margin = 2)["1", "1"]
p_pref <- prop.table(tab, margin = 2)["1", "0"]
n_ev   <- sum(tab[, "1"])
n_pref <- sum(tab[, "0"])

# Risk difference + Wald 95% CI
rd <- p_ev - p_pref
se_rd <- sqrt(p_ev * (1 - p_ev) / n_ev + p_pref * (1 - p_pref) / n_pref)
cat("Risk difference:", round(rd, 3), "\n")
cat("Wald 95% CI:", round(rd - 1.96 * se_rd, 3), "to", round(rd + 1.96 * se_rd, 3), "\n")

# Odds ratio + Fisher's exact two-sided 95% CI
fisher.test(tab)
```

\newpage

# Primary test 2 --- Delegation across repeated decisions

## Participant-level Wilcoxon--Mann--Whitney test

Preregistered one-sided WMW test on participant-average delegation
(paper: W = 6428, p = 0.243).

```{r wmw-test}
delegAv <- choices %>%
  filter(Part == 2) %>%
  group_by(Algorithm, ProlificID) %>%
  summarise(avDeleg = mean(Delegated, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Algorithm = factor(Algorithm, levels = c("Pref", "EV")))

wilcox.test(avDeleg ~ Algorithm, data = delegAv, alternative = "less")
```

## Effect size and CI for the WMW test

Rank-biserial correlation with a bootstrap 95% CI, as reported in the manuscript's new
Table 1 ($r_{rb} \approx 0.05$, bootstrap CI [-0.10, 0.20]).

```{r wmw-effectsize}
rank_biserial <- function(x, y) {
  n1 <- length(x); n2 <- length(y)
  U <- wilcox.test(x, y)$statistic
  1 - (2 * U) / (n1 * n2)
}

x_pref <- delegAv$avDeleg[delegAv$Algorithm == "Pref"]
x_ev   <- delegAv$avDeleg[delegAv$Algorithm == "EV"]

r_rb <- rank_biserial(x_pref, x_ev)
cat("Rank-biserial r:", round(r_rb, 3), "\n")

set.seed(1)
B <- 2000
boot_r <- replicate(B, {
  xb <- sample(x_pref, replace = TRUE)
  yb <- sample(x_ev,   replace = TRUE)
  rank_biserial(xb, yb)
})
cat("Bootstrap 95% CI:", round(quantile(boot_r, 0.025), 3), "to",
    round(quantile(boot_r, 0.975), 3), "\n")
```

```{r RA-distribution}
# calculate how often the EV-algorithm chooses p-bets
table(choicesP1$ChoiceType[choicesP1$OptionsetID <= 8] == "P105")
# 50-50; contrast that to...
pBetChoices <- choicesP1 %>%

  group_by(ProlificID) %>%

prop.table(table(pBetChoices > 0.5))
```

for 89.7% of the participants, the prefs-algorithm in expectation will produce fewer zero-outcomes than the EV-algorithm

## Preregistered regression specification

LPM with decision-set fixed effects and participant-clustered SEs. We first
construct the feedback-history regressor (running share of zero outcomes among
prior delegated choices).

```{r feedback-history}
choices <- choices %>%
  arrange(ProlificID, WithinPartDecisionNumber) %>%
  group_by(ProlificID) %>%
  mutate(
    delegated_round = (Delegated == 1),
    zero_payoff     = (RelevantPayoff == 0 & Delegated == 1),
    cum_delegated   = lag(cumsum(delegated_round), default = 0),
    cum_zero        = lag(cumsum(zero_payoff), default = 0),
    zero_rate       = ifelse(cum_delegated > 0, cum_zero / cum_delegated, NA)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r preregistered-regression}
# Preregistered model: treatment x (period + feedback history)
delRegPreReg <- feols(
  Delegated ~ EVAlgorithm * (WithinPartDecisionNumber + zero_rate) | OptionsetID,
  cluster = ~ProlificID,
  data = subset(choices, Part == 2)
)
summary(delRegPreReg)
```

## Robustness check: logistic regression

Re-estimating the preregistered LPM as a logistic regression with the same fixed
effects and cluster-robust SEs (paper: EVAlgorithm OR = 0.79, $p = 0.549$;
zero-outcome-history OR = 0.19, $p < 0.001$).

```{r logit-robustness}
delRegLogit <- feglm(
  Delegated ~ EVAlgorithm * (WithinPartDecisionNumber + zero_rate) | OptionsetID,
  family = "logit",
  cluster = ~ProlificID,
  data = subset(choices, Part == 2)
)
summary(delRegLogit)

# Odds ratios
exp(coef(delRegLogit))
```

## Supporting regression

Plain treatment effect (all rounds; excluding round 1; round 1 only). The
round-1-only LPM reproduces the Boschloo result
($\beta = 0.113$, one-sided $p = 0.041$).

```{r supporting-regression}
# 1st-round regression in the spirit of the preregistered model: treatment (fixing period to 1, and taking out the [non-existing] feedback history)
delRegPreReg <- feols(
  Delegated ~ EVAlgorithm | OptionsetID,
  cluster = ~ProlificID,
  data = subset(choices, Part == 2 & WithinPartDecisionNumber == 1)
)
summary(delRegPreReg) # Note: two-sided p-value
```

## Round-1 outcome and round-2 delegation, within treatment

The regression above is correlational across the whole sample. To probe the
feedback-driven account with variation that is not confounded by the between-treatment
difference in decision rule, we condition on having delegated in round 1 and compare
round-2 delegation after a zero vs. a positive round-1 payoff, separately by treatment
(the payoff depends on which lottery state was drawn). Paper: EV 36.0% vs. 64.8%
(two-sided Boschloo $p = 0.020$; OR = 0.31, 95% CI [0.10, 0.91] from Fisher's exact
test); Pref 50.0% vs. 72.5% (Boschloo $p = 0.078$; OR = 0.39, 95% CI [0.11, 1.29]).

```{r round1-outcome-round2-delegation}
round12 <- choices %>%
  filter(Part == 2, WithinPartDecisionNumber %in% 1:2) %>%
  select(ProlificID, EVAlgorithm, WithinPartDecisionNumber, Delegated, RelevantPayoff) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = WithinPartDecisionNumber,
              values_from = c(Delegated, RelevantPayoff)) %>%
  filter(Delegated_1 == 1, !is.na(Delegated_2)) %>%
  mutate(ZeroPayoff1 = factor(1 * (RelevantPayoff_1 == 0), levels = c(1, 0),
                              labels = c("zero", "positive")),
         Delegated2  = factor(Delegated_2, levels = c(1, 0),
                              labels = c("delegated", "not")))

for (trmt in c(1, 0)) {
  cat("\n====", ifelse(trmt == 1, "EV", "Preference-based"), "====\n")
  d <- filter(round12, EVAlgorithm == trmt)
  tab <- table(ZeroPayoff1 = d$ZeroPayoff1, Delegated2 = d$Delegated2)
  print(tab)
  print(round(prop.table(tab, margin = 1), 3))   # share delegating again
  # Paper: two-sided Boschloo p-value; Fisher's exact test supplies the odds ratio and CI
  cat("Two-sided Boschloo p =",
      round(exact.test(tab, method = "Boschloo", to.plot = FALSE)$p.value, 3), "\n")
  print(fisher.test(tab))
}
```

Do the two within-treatment contrasts differ from each other? (Paper: treatment-by-payoff
interaction in a logistic regression, $p = 0.772$.) Also, the share of round-1 delegators
who received a zero payoff is not lower under PREF (EV 25/79 = 31.6%; PREF 22/62 = 35.5%
among those with valid round-2 data); the weaker significance under PREF reflects the
smaller number of round-1 delegators (62 vs. 79), not fewer zero outcomes.

```{r round1-outcome-interaction}
round12_d <- round12 %>%
  mutate(Zero = 1 * (ZeroPayoff1 == "zero"),
         Del2 = 1 * (Delegated2 == "delegated"))
summary(glm(Del2 ~ EVAlgorithm * Zero, family = binomial, data = round12_d))$coefficients

round12_d %>%
  group_by(EVAlgorithm) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), zeroShare = mean(Zero))
```

what happens after non-delegation?

```{r round1-outcome-round2-nondelegation}
round12non <- choices %>%
  filter(Part == 2, WithinPartDecisionNumber %in% 1:2) %>%
  select(ProlificID, EVAlgorithm, WithinPartDecisionNumber, Delegated, RelevantPayoff) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = WithinPartDecisionNumber,
              values_from = c(Delegated, RelevantPayoff)) %>%
  filter(Delegated_1 == 0, !is.na(Delegated_2)) %>%
  mutate(ZeroPayoff1 = factor(1 * (RelevantPayoff_1 == 0), levels = c(1, 0),
                              labels = c("zero", "positive")),
         Delegated2  = factor(Delegated_2, levels = c(1, 0),
                              labels = c("delegated", "not")))

for (trmt in c(1, 0)) {
  cat("\n====", ifelse(trmt == 1, "EV", "Preference-based"), "====\n")
  nond <- filter(round12non, EVAlgorithm == trmt)
  nontab <- table(ZeroPayoff1 = nond$ZeroPayoff1, Delegated2 = nond$Delegated2)
  print(nontab)
  print(round(prop.table(nontab, margin = 1), 3))   # share delegating again
  cat("Two-sided Boschloo p =",
      round(exact.test(nontab, method = "Boschloo", to.plot = FALSE)$p.value, 3), "\n")
}
```

## Exploratory: why does delegation under EV decline after round 1?

The following chunks are exploratory and were not preregistered. They probe three
candidate explanations for the larger round-1-to-round-2 decline in delegation under the EV
algorithm: (i) differential exposure to zero payoffs, (ii) disappointment when the EV pick
differs from the participant's own Part-1 preference, and (iii) a first-contact difference
that is carried by a subgroup of never-delegators. Participant-clustered standard errors are
used throughout.

### (i) Exposure to zero payoffs

For each delegated decision we compute the probability that the algorithm's pick pays zero
(share of the ten equally likely states in which the option pays zero) and compare it with
the realized zero share. Paper: expected 41.7% (EV) vs. 34.8% (Pref); realized 40.3% vs.
36.2%, a difference of 4.1 percentage points (clustered $p = 0.18$).

```{r exposure-to-zeros}
# Payoff matrix of the Part-2 option sets, read from the raw decision-level file
raw_choices <- read.delim("260206_1528_537_lotteryChoices.xls")
state_cols  <- grep("^State", names(raw_choices), value = TRUE)

payoff_matrix <- raw_choices %>%
  filter(Part == 2, Option > 0, OptionsetID > 0) %>%
  select(OptionsetID, Option, all_of(state_cols)) %>%
  distinct(OptionsetID, Option, .keep_all = TRUE)
payoff_matrix$pZero <- rowMeans(payoff_matrix[, state_cols] == 0)

delegated_rounds <- choices %>%
  filter(Part == 2, Delegated == 1, Option > 0) %>%
  left_join(payoff_matrix %>% select(OptionsetID, Option, pZero),
            by = c("OptionsetID", "Option")) %>%
  mutate(Zero = 1 * (RelevantPayoff == 0))

delegated_rounds %>%
  group_by(Algorithm) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            participants = n_distinct(ProlificID),
            expectedZero = round(mean(pZero, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            realizedZero = round(mean(Zero), 3),
            .groups = "drop")

m_zero <- glm(Zero ~ EVAlgorithm, family = binomial, data = delegated_rounds)
coeftest(m_zero, vcov = vcovCL(m_zero, cluster = delegated_rounds$ProlificID))
```
### (ii) Does the EV pick match the participant's Part-1 preference?

Under the preference-based algorithm the delegated option is by construction the participant's
preferred option. Under EV it equals that option in about two thirds of delegated rounds. We
split EV delegations into "match" and "mismatch" and compare next-round delegation with the
preference-based group, with and without controlling for a zero payoff. Paper (all rounds
1--7, 799 delegated rounds): zero share 36.0% (Pref), 36.3% (EV match), 50.8% (EV mismatch);
next-round delegation 69.9%, 61.2%, 55.3%.

```{r mismatch-groups}
delegation_panel <- choices %>%
  filter(Part == 2) %>%
  arrange(ProlificID, WithinPartDecisionNumber) %>%
  group_by(ProlificID) %>%
  mutate(NextDelegated = lead(Delegated)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(Delegated == 1, !is.na(NextDelegated), NextDelegated >= 0) %>%
  mutate(Zero = 1 * (RelevantPayoff == 0),
         Group = factor(ifelse(EVAlgorithm == 0, "Pref",
                        ifelse(Option == PrefAlgoChoice, "EV_match", "EV_mismatch")),
                        levels = c("Pref", "EV_match", "EV_mismatch")))

# Logit with participant-clustered standard errors
cl_test <- function(formula, data) {
  m <- glm(formula, family = binomial, data = data)
  round(coeftest(m, vcov = vcovCL(m, cluster = data$ProlificID)), 3)
}

delegation_panel %>%
  group_by(Group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), zeroShare = round(mean(Zero), 3),
            nextDelegation = round(mean(NextDelegated), 3), .groups = "drop")

delegation_panel %>%
  group_by(Group, Zero) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), nextDelegation = round(mean(NextDelegated), 3), .groups = "drop")

cat("\n--- All rounds 1-7: groups only\n")
cl_test(NextDelegated ~ Group + WithinPartDecisionNumber, delegation_panel)
cat("\n--- All rounds 1-7: groups + zero payoff\n")
cl_test(NextDelegated ~ Group + Zero + WithinPartDecisionNumber, delegation_panel)
cat("\n--- Pooled EV coefficient without and with the zero control\n")
cl_test(NextDelegated ~ EVAlgorithm + WithinPartDecisionNumber, delegation_panel)
cl_test(NextDelegated ~ EVAlgorithm + Zero + WithinPartDecisionNumber, delegation_panel)

cat("\n--- Round 1 only: groups, groups + zero\n")
round1_panel <- filter(delegation_panel, WithinPartDecisionNumber == 1)
cl_test(NextDelegated ~ Group, round1_panel)
cl_test(NextDelegated ~ Group + Zero, round1_panel)

cat("\n--- Within EV: does a zero weigh more after a mismatched pick?\n")
ev_panel <- delegation_panel %>% filter(EVAlgorithm == 1) %>%
  mutate(Mismatch = 1 * (Group == "EV_mismatch"))
cl_test(NextDelegated ~ Zero * Mismatch + WithinPartDecisionNumber, ev_panel)

cat("\n--- Rough mediation arithmetic: zero coefficient x excess zero share\n")
b_zero <- coef(glm(NextDelegated ~ Group + Zero + WithinPartDecisionNumber,
                   family = binomial, data = delegation_panel))["Zero"]
zero_share <- tapply(delegation_panel$Zero, delegation_panel$Group, mean)
round(c(EV_match    = unname(b_zero * (zero_share["EV_match"]    - zero_share["Pref"])),
        EV_mismatch = unname(b_zero * (zero_share["EV_mismatch"] - zero_share["Pref"]))), 3)

cat("\n--- With task fixed effects (mismatch is not independent of the task)\n")
delegation_panel$Task <- factor(delegation_panel$OptionsetID)
cl_test(NextDelegated ~ Group + WithinPartDecisionNumber + Task, delegation_panel)[1:3, ]
cl_test(NextDelegated ~ Group + Zero + WithinPartDecisionNumber + Task, delegation_panel)[2:4, ]
m_zero_fe <- lm(Zero ~ Group + Task, data = delegation_panel)
cat("Zero share by group, task fixed effects (LPM):\n")
round(coeftest(m_zero_fe, vcov = vcovCL(m_zero_fe, cluster = delegation_panel$ProlificID))[2:3, ], 3)

cat("\n--- Counterfactual for round 1 -> round 2 (EV): what if round-1 EV delegators whose pick\n",
    "    differed from their preference had continued as often as those whose pick matched?\n")
r12_cf <- choices %>%
  filter(Part == 2, WithinPartDecisionNumber %in% 1:2) %>%
  mutate(Mismatch = 1 * (Option != PrefAlgoChoice)) %>%
  select(ProlificID, EVAlgorithm, WithinPartDecisionNumber, Delegated, Mismatch) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = WithinPartDecisionNumber, values_from = c(Delegated, Mismatch)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Delegated_1), !is.na(Delegated_2))
cf_stats <- function(d) {
  ev <- d[d$EVAlgorithm == 1, ]; pf <- d[d$EVAlgorithm == 0, ]
  chg <- function(x) mean(x$Delegated_2) - mean(x$Delegated_1)
  del <- ev[ev$Delegated_1 == 1, ]
  cont_match <- mean(del$Delegated_2[del$Mismatch_1 == 0])
  cont_mis   <- mean(del$Delegated_2[del$Mismatch_1 == 1])
  c(EV_change = chg(ev), Pref_change = chg(pf), difference = chg(ev) - chg(pf),
    n_mismatch = sum(del$Mismatch_1 == 1), cont_match = cont_match, cont_mismatch = cont_mis,
    shift_in_EV_round2 = sum(del$Mismatch_1 == 1) * (cont_match - cont_mis) / nrow(ev))
}
round(cf_stats(r12_cf), 3)
# Participant-level bootstrap interval for the shift (the share of the difference it
# accounts for is too imprecise to report)
set.seed(1)
by_id <- split(r12_cf, r12_cf$ProlificID)
boot_shift <- replicate(2000, cf_stats(do.call(rbind, by_id[sample(names(by_id), replace = TRUE)]))["shift_in_EV_round2"])
round(quantile(boot_shift, c(.025, .5, .975), na.rm = TRUE), 3)
```

#### Forgone payoffs

The feedback screen showed the payoffs of all options in the drawn state, so participants could
see what another option would have paid. We compute the gap between the best available option
and the realized payoff ("regret", in units of 100 points) and ask whether it predicts
next-round delegation beyond a zero payoff. Paper (all rounds 1--7): regret alone is
negative ($-0.131$, $p < 0.001$) but drops to $+0.014$ ($p = 0.74$) once the zero payoff is
included. Option 3 of option set 5 never appears in the data, so for that set the best
available option may be slightly understated.

```{r regret-forgone}
payoff_by_set <- split(payoff_matrix, payoff_matrix$OptionsetID)
best_available <- function(set, state) {
  if (is.na(state) || state < 1) return(NA_real_)
  max(payoff_by_set[[as.character(set)]][[state_cols[state]]])
}
regret_panel <- delegation_panel %>%
  mutate(BestAvailable = mapply(best_available, OptionsetID, PayoffRelevantState),
         Regret = (BestAvailable - RelevantPayoff) / 100)

regret_panel %>%
  group_by(Algorithm) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), meanRegret = round(mean(Regret, na.rm = TRUE), 2), .groups = "drop")

cat("\n--- Regret alone, then regret + zero payoff\n")
cl_test(NextDelegated ~ EVAlgorithm + Regret + WithinPartDecisionNumber, regret_panel)
cl_test(NextDelegated ~ EVAlgorithm + Zero + Regret + WithinPartDecisionNumber, regret_panel)
```

#### Percentage-point version of the match/mismatch comparison

The paper reports these comparisons as percentage-point differences from linear probability
models with participant-clustered standard errors. Paper: matching EV picks $-8.4$ points
(95% CI [$-18.7$, 2.0], $p = 0.112$) and mismatching EV picks $-14.5$ points (95% CI
[$-26.9$, $-2.0$], $p = 0.023$) relative to preference-based delegation; mismatching vs.
matching EV picks $-6.1$ points ($p = 0.266$); with task fixed effects $-16.4$ points
($p = 0.012$) for mismatching picks; controlling for a zero payoff $-10.8$ points
($p = 0.078$); a zero payoff within EV lowers continued delegation by 20.0 points after a
matching and by 36.7 points after a mismatching pick (difference 16.7 points, $p = 0.083$).

```{r mismatch-lpm}
lpm_pp <- function(formula, data, terms) {
  m  <- lm(formula, data = data)
  V  <- vcovCL(m, cluster = data$ProlificID)
  ct <- coeftest(m, vcov = V)
  ci <- coefci(m, vcov. = V)
  round(cbind(pp = 100 * ct[terms, 1], lo = 100 * ci[terms, 1], hi = 100 * ci[terms, 2],
              p = ct[terms, 4]), 3)
}
delegation_panel$Task <- factor(delegation_panel$OptionsetID)
lpm_pp(NextDelegated ~ Group + WithinPartDecisionNumber, delegation_panel,
       c("GroupEV_match", "GroupEV_mismatch"))
lpm_pp(NextDelegated ~ Group + WithinPartDecisionNumber + Task, delegation_panel,
       c("GroupEV_match", "GroupEV_mismatch"))
lpm_pp(NextDelegated ~ Group + Zero + WithinPartDecisionNumber, delegation_panel,
       c("GroupEV_match", "GroupEV_mismatch", "Zero"))

cat("\nMismatching vs. matching EV picks\n")
delegation_panel$GroupRef <- relevel(delegation_panel$Group, ref = "EV_match")
lpm_pp(NextDelegated ~ GroupRef + WithinPartDecisionNumber, delegation_panel, "GroupRefEV_mismatch")

cat("\nWithin EV: zero payoff x mismatching pick\n")
ev_lpm <- delegation_panel %>% filter(EVAlgorithm == 1) %>%
  mutate(Mismatch = 1 * (Group == "EV_mismatch"))
lpm_pp(NextDelegated ~ Zero * Mismatch + WithinPartDecisionNumber, ev_lpm,
       c("Zero", "Mismatch", "Zero:Mismatch"))

cat("\nPooled EV gap without and with the zero control\n")
lpm_pp(NextDelegated ~ EVAlgorithm + WithinPartDecisionNumber, delegation_panel, "EVAlgorithm")
lpm_pp(NextDelegated ~ EVAlgorithm + Zero + WithinPartDecisionNumber, delegation_panel,
       c("EVAlgorithm", "Zero"))
```

### (iii) The first-contact gap sits at the opt-out margin

The framework predicts that resistance is concentrated in participants who value choice
authority and opt out categorically. We first compare round-1 delegation among participants who
delegate at least once. Paper: 65.6% (Pref) vs. 69.3% (EV), one-sided Boschloo $p = 0.289$.
Because never-delegation is defined over all eight rounds and thus includes round 1, we then
repeat the comparison with "otherwise-never-delegators", defined without the round(s) under
analysis: for round 1, participants who never delegate in rounds 2--8; for the rounds 1--2
analysis, participants who never delegate in rounds 3--8. Paper (round 1): 16.8% (Pref) vs.
7.6% (EV), one-sided Boschloo $p = 0.019$; round-1 delegation among all
other participants 64.9% vs. 67.9% (one-sided $p = 0.330$). The comparisons are descriptive, since they
condition on later behaviour. We do not report a numerical split of the 11.2-point gap,
because the within-group part rests on only 28 otherwise-never-delegators.

```{r subgroup-accounting}
wide <- choices %>%
  filter(Part == 2) %>%
  select(ProlificID, EVAlgorithm, WithinPartDecisionNumber, Delegated) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = WithinPartDecisionNumber, values_from = Delegated,
              names_prefix = "d")
dmat <- as.matrix(wide[, paste0("d", 1:8)])

# 1 if the participant never delegates in the given rounds (NA if no valid decision there)
never_in <- function(cols) {
  x <- dmat[, cols, drop = FALSE]
  ifelse(rowSums(!is.na(x)) == 0, NA, 1 * (rowSums(x, na.rm = TRUE) == 0))
}
wide$Never              <- never_in(1:8)   # standard definition (all rounds)
wide$OtherwiseNever_r1  <- never_in(2:8)   # for analyses of round 1
wide$OtherwiseNever_r12 <- never_in(3:8)   # for analyses of rounds 1 and 2
wide$lateRate <- rowSums(dmat[, 2:8, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE) /
                 rowSums(!is.na(dmat[, 2:8, drop = FALSE]))

# Boschloo exact test on a 2 x 2 table built from two groups (Pref = 0, EV = 1)
boschloo_p <- function(outcome, group, alternative = "two.sided") {
  tab <- table(factor(group, levels = c(0, 1)), factor(outcome, levels = c(1, 0)))
  exact.test(tab, method = "Boschloo", alternative = alternative, to.plot = FALSE)$p.value
}

cat("--- Plain definition: participants who delegate at least once\n")
not_never <- filter(wide, Never == 0, !is.na(d1))
not_never %>%
  group_by(EVAlgorithm) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), round1 = round(100 * mean(d1), 1),
            rounds2to8 = round(100 * mean(lateRate, na.rm = TRUE), 1), .groups = "drop")
# one-sided: EV delegates more than Pref ("less" = first row, Pref, has the lower share)
cat("Round-1 delegation, EV > Pref (one-sided Boschloo p):",
    round(boschloo_p(not_never$d1, not_never$EVAlgorithm, "less"), 3), "\n")

cat("\n--- Robustness: otherwise-never-delegators (never in rounds 2-8)\n")
A <- filter(wide, !is.na(d1), !is.na(OtherwiseNever_r1))
A %>%
  group_by(EVAlgorithm) %>%
  summarise(N = n(),
            nOtherwiseNever       = sum(OtherwiseNever_r1),
            pctOtherwiseNever     = round(100 * mean(OtherwiseNever_r1), 1),
            round1_others         = round(100 * mean(d1[OtherwiseNever_r1 == 0]), 1),
            round1_otherwiseNever = round(100 * mean(d1[OtherwiseNever_r1 == 1]), 1),
            .groups = "drop")
cat("Share of otherwise-never-delegators, Pref > EV (one-sided Boschloo p):",
    round(boschloo_p(A$OtherwiseNever_r1, A$EVAlgorithm, "greater"), 3), "\n")
cat("  two-sided:", round(boschloo_p(A$OtherwiseNever_r1, A$EVAlgorithm), 3), "\n")
others1 <- filter(A, OtherwiseNever_r1 == 0)
cat("Round-1 delegation among all others, EV > Pref (one-sided Boschloo p):",
    round(boschloo_p(others1$d1, others1$EVAlgorithm, "less"), 3), "\n")
```

### Does the round-1 to round-2 decline differ between conditions?

Descriptively the EV decline is larger, but the difference-in-differences is imprecise.
Paper: round 1 vs. round 2 interaction clustered $p = 0.14$; round 1 vs. rounds 2--8
interaction $p = 0.050$. We report both as exploratory and do not read the first as evidence
that the two declines are equal. Among participants who delegate at least once in rounds 3--8
(the analysed rounds do not enter this definition), the round 1 to round 2 change is $-5.8$
points (Pref) vs. $-14.5$ points (EV); the interaction is $-0.36$ ($p = 0.38$).

```{r decline-did}
round12_all <- choices %>%
  filter(Part == 2, WithinPartDecisionNumber %in% 1:2) %>%
  mutate(Round2 = 1 * (WithinPartDecisionNumber == 2))
cl_test(Delegated ~ EVAlgorithm * Round2, round12_all)

round1_vs_rest <- choices %>%
  filter(Part == 2) %>%
  mutate(Round1 = 1 * (WithinPartDecisionNumber == 1))
cl_test(Delegated ~ EVAlgorithm * Round1, round1_vs_rest)

# Share of otherwise-never-delegators (rounds 3-8) and the decline among all others
E <- filter(wide, !is.na(d1), !is.na(d2), !is.na(OtherwiseNever_r12))
E %>%
  group_by(EVAlgorithm) %>%
  summarise(N = n(), pctOtherwiseNever = round(100 * mean(OtherwiseNever_r12), 1),
            .groups = "drop")
cat("Share of otherwise-never-delegators (rounds 3-8), Pref > EV (one-sided Boschloo p):",
    round(boschloo_p(E$OtherwiseNever_r12, E$EVAlgorithm, "greater"), 3), "\n")

others12 <- filter(E, OtherwiseNever_r12 == 0)
others12 %>%
  group_by(EVAlgorithm) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), round1 = round(100 * mean(d1), 1), round2 = round(100 * mean(d2), 1),
            change = round(round2 - round1, 1), .groups = "drop")
others12_long <- others12 %>%
  select(ProlificID, EVAlgorithm, d1, d2) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(d1, d2), names_to = "round", values_to = "Delegated") %>%
  mutate(Round2 = 1 * (round == "d2"))
cl_test(Delegated ~ EVAlgorithm * Round2, others12_long)

# Does the round-1 choice predict later delegation differently by condition?
later <- choices %>%
  filter(Part == 2, WithinPartDecisionNumber >= 2) %>%
  left_join(choices %>% filter(Part == 2, WithinPartDecisionNumber == 1) %>%
              select(ProlificID, D1 = Delegated), by = "ProlificID") %>%
  filter(!is.na(D1))
later %>% group_by(Algorithm, D1) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), delegationRate = round(mean(Delegated), 3), .groups = "drop")
cl_test(Delegated ~ D1 * EVAlgorithm, later)
```

# Categorical non-delegation

We classify participants as never-, sometimes-, or always-delegators and
compare never-delegation across conditions (paper: 15.7% Pref vs. 3.4% EV).

```{r delegator-types}
choices <- choices %>%
  group_by(ProlificID) %>%
  mutate(sumDelegations = sum(Delegated)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(
    prolificData %>% select(Participant.id, TimeInSeconds = Time.taken),
    by = c("ProlificID" = "Participant.id")
  )

analysis_data <- choices %>%
  group_by(ProlificID) %>%
  summarise(
    EVAlgorithm                 = first(EVAlgorithm),
    sumDelegations              = first(sumDelegations),
    Female                      = first(Female),
    Age                         = first(Age),
    HHIncome                    = first(HHIncome),
    Education                   = first(Education),
    ProbOfBadComputerChoices    = first(ProbOfBadComputerChoices),
    ProbOfAbsurdComputerChoices = first(ProbOfAbsurdComputerChoices),
    ComputerRiskTaking          = first(ComputerRiskTaking),
    PBetChoices                 = first(PBet_count),
    TimeInSeconds               = first(TimeInSeconds),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    DelegationGroup = ifelse(sumDelegations == 0, "Never", "AtLeastOnce"),
    NonDelegator    = 1 * (sumDelegations == 0),
    DelegatorType   = factor(
      if_else(sumDelegations == 0, "NeverDelegator",
              if_else(sumDelegations == 8, "AlwaysDelegator", "SometimesDelegator")),
      levels = c("NeverDelegator", "SometimesDelegator", "AlwaysDelegator")
    )
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    subjects %>% select(ProlificID, RiskTaking, FinMarketExperience,
                        FinanciallyResponsible, AIXperience, Reliable),
    by = "ProlificID"
  )

# Distribution of delegator types by condition (column 2 = EV)
table(analysis_data$DelegatorType, analysis_data$EVAlgorithm)
prop.table(table(analysis_data$DelegatorType, analysis_data$EVAlgorithm), margin = 2)
```

## Significance test and effect size for categorical non-delegation

Main test: one-sided Boschloo exact test (Pref > EV) with the two treatment arms as
the binomial groups. The outcome was not preregistered; a one-sided test is in line
with the general prediction that personalization reduces acceptance, and it is the
same test as for the earlier study in the footnote. The two-sided Boschloo test,
Fisher's exact test (used for the odds ratio and its CI), and the risk difference with
Wald 95% CI are reported alongside (paper: one-sided $p < 0.001$, two-sided
$p = 0.001$; RD = 12.3pp [4.9, 19.7]; OR = 5.25 [1.65, 22.07]).

```{r nondelegation-significance}
# Rows: treatment arms (the binomial groups); columns: never-delegator yes / no
nondeleg_tab <- table(
  Treatment    = factor(analysis_data$EVAlgorithm, levels = c(0, 1),
                        labels = c("Pref", "EV")),
  NonDelegator = factor(analysis_data$NonDelegator, levels = c(1, 0),
                        labels = c("Never", "NotNever"))
)
nondeleg_tab

# Main test: one-sided Boschloo (Pref > EV)
exact.test(nondeleg_tab, method = "Boschloo", alternative = "greater",
           to.plot = FALSE)$p.value
# Two-sided, for reference
exact.test(nondeleg_tab, method = "Boschloo", to.plot = FALSE)$p.value

# Odds ratio and its CI (Fisher's exact; expect OR ~ 5.25)
fisher.test(nondeleg_tab)

# Risk difference + Wald 95% CI
p_pref_nd <- nondeleg_tab["Pref", "Never"] / sum(nondeleg_tab["Pref", ])
p_ev_nd   <- nondeleg_tab["EV",   "Never"] / sum(nondeleg_tab["EV", ])
n_pref_nd <- sum(nondeleg_tab["Pref", ])
n_ev_nd   <- sum(nondeleg_tab["EV", ])
rd_nd     <- p_pref_nd - p_ev_nd
se_rd_nd  <- sqrt(p_pref_nd * (1 - p_pref_nd) / n_pref_nd +
                  p_ev_nd * (1 - p_ev_nd) / n_ev_nd)
cat("Risk difference:", round(rd_nd, 3), "\n")
cat("Wald 95% CI:", round(rd_nd - 1.96 * se_rd_nd, 3), "to",
    round(rd_nd + 1.96 * se_rd_nd, 3), "\n")
```

The tests below are in the order in which they appear in the text (Results,
"Categorical non-delegation"); never-delegators are compared with participants who
delegated at least once. Tests that are *not* reported in the text are collected in a
separate subsection further below.

```{r nondelegator-tests}
# Age (the text lists never-delegators first: 41.8 vs. 42.9, t = -0.329)

       data = analysis_data)

)
female_table
exact.test(female_table[, c("0", "1")], method = "Boschloo", to.plot = FALSE)$p.value
```

## Choice quality among never-delegators (Limitations)

Tests whether never-delegators' non-dominated choice rate among their self-made
Part-2 decisions differs from that of participants who delegated at least once, used
in the manuscript to argue against a task-difficulty confound for categorical
non-delegation (paper: 34.7% vs. 33.6%; Welch $t = -0.25$, $p = 0.806$; Wilcoxon
$p = 0.669$).

**Note on the sample sizes.** The first table counts *decisions* and the second
*participants*, so the numbers differ by construction. The 22 never-delegators made
175 self-chosen decisions in total (22 x 8 = 176 minus one round without a valid
decision). The 170 in the participant-level comparison is the number of participants
who delegated at least once *and* made at least one valid decision themselves: of the
211 participants who delegated at least once, 40 delegated in every valid round (38 in
all 8 rounds, 2 with fewer valid rounds) and 1 has only a timed-out own decision, so
they contribute no self-chosen decision (211 - 41 = 170).

```{r choicequality-by-nondelegator}
selfchoice <- choices %>%
  filter(Part == 2, Delegated == 0, Option > 0) %>%
  left_join(
    analysis_data %>% select(ProlificID, DelegatorType, DelegationGroup),
    by = "ProlificID"
  )

# Decision level, by delegator type (n_decisions = self-chosen decisions,
# n_participants = participants contributing to them)
selfchoice %>%
  group_by(DelegatorType) %>%
  summarise(avNonDom = mean(Nondominated, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_decisions = n(),
            n_participants = n_distinct(ProlificID), .groups = "drop")

# Participant level: average non-dominated rate, Never vs. AtLeastOnce
partavg <- selfchoice %>%
  group_by(ProlificID, DelegationGroup) %>%
  summarise(Nondominated = mean(Nondominated, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

partavg %>%
  group_by(DelegationGroup) %>%
  summarise(Nondominated = mean(Nondominated), n_participants = n(), .groups = "drop")

t.test(Nondominated ~ DelegationGroup, data = partavg)
wilcox.test(Nondominated ~ DelegationGroup, data = partavg)
```

# Responses to feedback

## Preregistered secondary hypothesis: switching to non-delegation after a zero payoff

The preregistration (question 8) contains one secondary hypothesis: after delegating
to the algorithm with a 0-payoff, participants in PREF are more likely to switch to
non-delegation in the following round than under any other circumstances, in
particular than under the same circumstances in the EV condition. The preregistration
does not specify a test. We estimate an LPM of switching to non-delegation in rounds
2--8 that follow a delegated round, with task and decision-number fixed effects and
participant-clustered SEs; the preregistered prediction corresponds to a *positive*
`PREF x ZeroPayoff` interaction (tested one-sided). Note that lags are taken over the
available rows of a participant (16 of the 1,864 Part-2 rounds have no valid
decision and are dropped, which affects 13 participants).

```{r preregistered-switching}
switchdat <- choices %>%
  filter(Part == 2) %>%
  group_by(ProlificID) %>%
  arrange(WithinPartDecisionNumber, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(lagDelegated = lag(Delegated, 1),
         lagPayoff    = lag(RelevantPayoff, 1)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(WithinPartDecisionNumber > 1, !is.na(lagDelegated)) %>%
  mutate(PREF         = 1 - EVAlgorithm,
         ZeroPayoff   = 1 * (lagPayoff == 0),
         SwitchToNon  = 1 * (lagDelegated == 1 & Delegated == 0))

# Rounds that follow a delegated round (paper: 799 observations, 209 participants)
afterDeleg <- filter(switchdat, lagDelegated == 1)
c(N = nrow(afterDeleg), participants = n_distinct(afterDeleg$ProlificID))

# Raw switching rates (paper: EV 30.3% / 55.6%; PREF 21.5% / 45.3%)
afterDeleg %>%
  group_by(PREF, ZeroPayoff) %>%
  summarise(rate = mean(SwitchToNon), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

switchReg <- feols(
  SwitchToNon ~ PREF * ZeroPayoff | OptionsetID + WithinPartDecisionNumber,
  cluster = ~ProlificID, data = afterDeleg
)
summary(switchReg)

# One-sided p-value for the preregistered direction (interaction > 0);
# paper: beta = -0.023, SE = 0.067, one-sided p = 0.633 (two-sided 0.734)
ct <- coeftable(switchReg)
pt(ct["PREF:ZeroPayoff", "t value"],
   df = n_distinct(afterDeleg$ProlificID) - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
```

Supplementary contrasts reported in the text: (a) only rounds following a zero-payoff
delegation, PREF vs. EV (paper: beta = -0.105, SE = 0.070, two-sided p = 0.140); (b) the
zero-payoff effect within each condition (paper: 0.254 in EV, 0.250 in PREF, both
$p < 0.001$); (c) comparison with *all* other rounds 2--8 as the reference
(paper: interaction beta = -0.071, SE = 0.071, one-sided p = 0.840; 1,615 observations).

```{r preregistered-switching-contrasts}
# (a) after zero-payoff delegation only
feols(SwitchToNon ~ PREF | OptionsetID + WithinPartDecisionNumber,
      cluster = ~ProlificID, data = filter(afterDeleg, ZeroPayoff == 1)) %>% summary()

# (b) zero vs. positive payoff after delegation, by condition
feols(SwitchToNon ~ ZeroPayoff | OptionsetID + WithinPartDecisionNumber,
      cluster = ~ProlificID, data = filter(afterDeleg, PREF == 0)) %>% summary()  # EV
feols(SwitchToNon ~ ZeroPayoff | OptionsetID + WithinPartDecisionNumber,
      cluster = ~ProlificID, data = filter(afterDeleg, PREF == 1)) %>% summary()  # PREF

# (c) "any other circumstances" = all rounds 2--8
switchAll <- switchdat %>% mutate(ZeroAfterDeleg = 1 * (lagDelegated == 1 & lagPayoff == 0))
switchRegAll <- feols(
  SwitchToNon ~ PREF * ZeroAfterDeleg | OptionsetID + WithinPartDecisionNumber,
  cluster = ~ProlificID, data = switchAll
)
summary(switchRegAll)
ctA <- coeftable(switchRegAll)
pt(ctA["PREF:ZeroAfterDeleg", "t value"],
   df = n_distinct(switchAll$ProlificID) - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
```

## Exploratory: win-stay / lose-shift

Not preregistered. Win-stay/lose-shift model on rounds 2--8 (paper, Section "Responses
to feedback"), and its decomposition by who produced the previous outcome.

```{r win-stay-lose-shift}
choices <- choices %>%
  group_by(ProlificID) %>%
  arrange(WithinPartDecisionNumber, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    lagDelegated          = lag(Delegated, 1),
    lagRelevantPayoff     = lag(RelevantPayoff, 1),
    lagSatisfactionRating = lag(SatisfactionRating, 1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

choices$stay <- 1 * (choices$Delegated == choices$lagDelegated)
# The paper models SWITCHING (= 1 - stay), so that a positive coefficient always means more switching
choices$switch <- 1 - choices$stay

# "Prior win": the outcome of the PREVIOUS round was strictly positive.
# (lagWin is defined from the lagged payoff, i.e. the genuine win-stay/lose-shift
# notion of reacting to the previously experienced outcome.)
choices$lagWin <- 1 * (choices$lagRelevantPayoff > 0)

# Pooled model: treatment x prior win
winStayReg <- feols(
  switch ~ EVAlgorithm * lagWin | OptionsetID + WithinPartDecisionNumber,
  cluster = ~ProlificID,
  data = subset(choices, Part == 2 & WithinPartDecisionNumber > 1)
)
summary(winStayReg)

# Appendix table: the EV coefficient is the EV-vs-Pref difference in staying after a
# loss (lagWin = 0); adding the interaction gives the difference after a win
b <- coef(winStayReg); V <- vcov(winStayReg)
gap_win <- b["EVAlgorithm"] + b["EVAlgorithm:lagWin"]
se_win  <- sqrt(V["EVAlgorithm", "EVAlgorithm"] +
                V["EVAlgorithm:lagWin", "EVAlgorithm:lagWin"] +
                2 * V["EVAlgorithm", "EVAlgorithm:lagWin"])
cat("EV vs. Pref after a win:", round(gap_win, 3), " SE", round(se_win, 3),
    " p", round(2 * pnorm(-abs(gap_win / se_win)), 3), "\n")
```

Separately by treatment, distinguishing whether the previous round was
delegated (`lagDelegated == 1`, i.e. "the algorithm" produced the outcome) from
a self-made choice. This separates lose-shift after one's own loss from
lose-shift after a delegated (algorithmic) loss.

```{r win-stay-by-treatment}
# EV condition
winStayReg_EV <- feols(
  switch ~ lagDelegated * I(1 - lagWin) | OptionsetID + WithinPartDecisionNumber,
  cluster = ~ProlificID,
  data = subset(choices, EVAlgorithm == 1 & Part == 2 & WithinPartDecisionNumber > 1)
)
summary(winStayReg_EV)

# Preference-based condition
winStayReg_Pref <- feols(
  switch ~ lagDelegated * I(1 - lagWin) | OptionsetID + WithinPartDecisionNumber,
  cluster = ~ProlificID,
  data = subset(choices, EVAlgorithm == 0 & Part == 2 & WithinPartDecisionNumber > 1)
)
summary(winStayReg_Pref)
```

```{r win-stay-rates}
# Average stay rates by condition, prior delegation, and prior win/loss
choices %>%
  filter(Part == 2, WithinPartDecisionNumber > 1) %>%
  group_by(EVAlgorithm, lagDelegated, lagWin) %>%
  summarise(avg_stay_rate = mean(stay, na.rm = TRUE),
            avg_switch_rate = mean(switch, na.rm = TRUE),
            n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(EVAlgorithm, lagDelegated, lagWin)
```

## Treatment comparison of expected algorithmic errors

Formal comparison of expected non-preferred and completely weird choices across
treatments. A LOWER expected number of non-preferred choices under the
preference-based algorithm would indicate that participants believe the
personalized algorithm is doing its job (matching their preferences).

```{r expectations-comparison}
expect_tbl <- subjects %>%
  mutate(Condition = ifelse(EVAlgorithm == 1, "EV", "Preference-based")) %>%
  group_by(Condition) %>%
  summarise(
    n                  = n(),
    mean_nonpreferred  = mean(ProbOfBadComputerChoices, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_nonpreferred    = sd(ProbOfBadComputerChoices, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_weird         = mean(ProbOfAbsurdComputerChoices, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_weird           = sd(ProbOfAbsurdComputerChoices, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
expect_tbl

# Expected NON-PREFERRED choices: EV vs. Preference-based
t.test(ProbOfBadComputerChoices ~ EVAlgorithm, data = subjects)
wilcox.test(ProbOfBadComputerChoices ~ EVAlgorithm, data = subjects)

# Expected COMPLETELY WEIRD choices: EV vs. Preference-based
t.test(ProbOfAbsurdComputerChoices ~ EVAlgorithm, data = subjects)
wilcox.test(ProbOfAbsurdComputerChoices ~ EVAlgorithm, data = subjects)

# Within the preference-based condition: do never-delegators expect the
# personalized algorithm to make MORE non-preferred choices than delegators?
# (If not, categorical non-delegation is not driven by distrust in the
#  algorithm's ability to capture one's preferences.)
analysis_data %>%
  filter(EVAlgorithm == 0) %>%
  group_by(NonDelegator) %>%
  summarise(
    n                 = n(),
    mean_nonpreferred = mean(ProbOfBadComputerChoices, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

t.test(ProbOfBadComputerChoices ~ NonDelegator,
       data = subset(analysis_data, EVAlgorithm == 0))
```

### Side note: participants who expect few mistakes by the algorithm

The paper notes that restricting the sample to participants who expect at most two
non-preferred choices out of ten (about 21% of the sample) leaves the treatment differences
at least as large. The subgroups are small, and the restriction conditions on a post-task
measure, so we regard this only as a robustness remark. Paper (at most 2): round-1
delegation 100% (EV, n = 15) vs. 72.7% (Pref, n = 33), one-sided Boschloo $p = 0.012$;
never-delegation 0 of 15 vs. 6 of 33 ($p = 0.053$). With a cut-off of 3: 83.3% vs. 65.4%
($p = 0.064$) and never-delegation $p = 0.039$.

```{r few-mistakes-expected}
few_mistakes <- subjects %>%
  inner_join(choices %>% filter(Part == 2) %>% group_by(ProlificID) %>%
               summarise(k = sum(Delegated == 1), n = sum(Delegated >= 0),
                         d1 = Delegated[WithinPartDecisionNumber == 1][1], .groups = "drop"),
             by = "ProlificID")

# one-sided Boschloo on arms (row 1 = EV, row 2 = Pref); "greater" = EV higher
boschloo_ev <- function(x, ev, alternative) {
  tab <- rbind(c(sum(x[ev == 1] == 1), sum(x[ev == 1] == 0)),
               c(sum(x[ev == 0] == 1), sum(x[ev == 0] == 0)))
  exact.test(tab, method = "Boschloo", alternative = alternative, to.plot = FALSE)$p.value
}
for (cutoff in c(2, 3)) {
  d <- filter(few_mistakes, ProbOfBadComputerChoices <= cutoff, !is.na(d1))
  cat(sprintf("\n--- At most %d expected non-preferred choices: n = %d (%.1f%% of %d)\n",
              cutoff, nrow(d), 100 * nrow(d) / nrow(few_mistakes), nrow(few_mistakes)))
  print(d %>% group_by(EVAlgorithm) %>%
          summarise(n = n(), round1 = round(100 * mean(d1), 1), never = sum(k == 0),
                    neverPct = round(100 * mean(k == 0), 1),
                    avgDelegation = round(100 * mean(k / n), 1), .groups = "drop"))
  cat("Round-1 delegation, EV > Pref (one-sided Boschloo p):",
      round(boschloo_ev(d$d1, d$EVAlgorithm, "greater"), 3), "\n")
  cat("Never-delegation, Pref > EV (one-sided Boschloo p):",
      round(boschloo_ev(1 * (d$k == 0), d$EVAlgorithm, "less"), 3), "\n")
}
```

## Aggregate reason patterns

In-text figures for performance, distrust, and responsibility motives by
delegation type (delegators vs. never-delegators).

```{r reasons-aggregate}
subjects_long %>%
  group_by(sumDeleg0, item) %>%
  summarise(rate = mean(clicked, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sumDeleg0, values_from = rate) %>%
  rename(Delegators = `FALSE`, NeverDelegators = `TRUE`)
```
## The responsibility items are worded according to the hypothetical choice

The reason items refer to the hypothetical choice (`DelegateHyp10`: 1 = delegate, 0 = decide
oneself) and their wording depends on it. For example, `Responsibility4Choice` reads "I wanted
to be responsible for choosing the option" for participants who chose to decide themselves
and "I didn't want to be responsible for choosing the option" for participants who chose to
delegate. The pooled comparison of never-delegators with the rest therefore largely contrasts
reasons for deciding oneself with reasons for delegating. This section documents the
relationship between the hypothetical choice and actual behavior and reports the endorsement
rates within each hypothetical choice. Paper: 91% of never-delegators decide themselves,
95% of always-delegators delegate, Spearman correlation with the Part-2 delegation share
0.68; endorsement of `Responsibility4Choice` is 66.4% among participants who decide
themselves and 16.2% among those who delegate; never-delegators who decide themselves do not
differ from other participants who decide themselves (70.0% vs. 65.6%; Boschloo
$p = 0.80$); about one in four delegators endorses either responsibility item.

```{r responsibility-by-hypothetical-choice}
resp <- subjects2 %>%
  left_join(choices %>% filter(Part == 2) %>% group_by(ProlificID) %>%
              summarise(nValid = sum(Delegated >= 0),
                        delegShare = mean(Delegated[Delegated >= 0]), .groups = "drop"),
            by = "ProlificID") %>%
  mutate(Type = ifelse(sumDelegations == 0, "Never",
                ifelse(sumDelegations == nValid, "Always", "Sometimes")),
         Hypothetical = ifelse(DelegateHyp10 == 1, "Delegate", "Decide myself"))

cat("Hypothetical choice by actual delegation type\n")
table(Hypothetical = resp$Hypothetical, Type = resp$Type)
cat("\nColumn percentages\n")
round(100 * prop.table(table(resp$Hypothetical, resp$Type), 2), 1)

cat("\nMean Part-2 delegation share by hypothetical choice\n")
resp %>% group_by(Hypothetical) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), meanShare = round(mean(delegShare), 3), .groups = "drop")
cat("Spearman correlation, delegation share vs. hypothetical choice:",
    round(cor(resp$delegShare, resp$DelegateHyp10, method = "spearman"), 3), "\n")
sometimes <- filter(resp, Type == "Sometimes")
cat("  among sometimes-delegators only:",
    round(cor(sometimes$delegShare, sometimes$DelegateHyp10, method = "spearman"), 3), "\n")

cat("\nResponsibility items by hypothetical choice (percent endorsing)\n")
resp %>%
  group_by(Hypothetical) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            Responsibility4Choice  = round(100 * mean(Responsibility4Choice == 1, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            Responsibility4Outcome = round(100 * mean(Responsibility4Outcome == 1, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            .groups = "drop")

cat("\nAmong participants who chose to delegate: either responsibility item\n")
deleg_hyp <- filter(resp, DelegateHyp10 == 1)
cat("  n =", nrow(deleg_hyp), " share =",
    round(100 * mean(deleg_hyp$Responsibility4Choice == 1 |
                     deleg_hyp$Responsibility4Outcome == 1, na.rm = TRUE), 1), "%\n")

cat("\nResponsibility4Choice by actual type and hypothetical choice\n")
resp %>%
  group_by(Type, Hypothetical) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), pct = round(100 * mean(Responsibility4Choice == 1, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            .groups = "drop")

cat("\nWithin participants who decide themselves: never-delegators vs. others (Boschloo)\n")
own <- filter(resp, DelegateHyp10 == 0)
tab_own <- table(factor(1 * (own$Type == "Never"), levels = c(1, 0)),
                 factor(own$Responsibility4Choice, levels = c(1, 0)))
print(tab_own)
cat("  two-sided Boschloo p =",
    round(exact.test(tab_own, method = "Boschloo", to.plot = FALSE)$p.value, 3), "\n")

cat("\nTreatment differences within each hypothetical choice (Responsibility4Choice)\n")
for (h in c("Delegate", "Decide myself")) {
  d <- filter(resp, Hypothetical == h)
  tb <- table(factor(d$EVAlgorithm, levels = c(0, 1)),
              factor(d$Responsibility4Choice, levels = c(1, 0)))
  cat(" ", h, ": Pref", round(100 * mean(d$Responsibility4Choice[d$EVAlgorithm == 0] == 1), 1),
      "% vs. EV", round(100 * mean(d$Responsibility4Choice[d$EVAlgorithm == 1] == 1), 1),
      "%; Boschloo p =", round(exact.test(tb, method = "Boschloo", to.plot = FALSE)$p.value, 3), "\n")
}
```




## Reasons among delegators, by treatment

The paper notes that, among participants who delegated at least once, the selected reasons
differ little by treatment (by at most 8 percentage points; smallest two-sided Boschloo
$p = 0.214$). The four EV never-delegators are too few to compare.

```{r reasons-by-treatment-delegators}
delegator_reasons <- subjects2 %>% filter(sumDeleg0 == FALSE)
items_closed <- c("DontTrust", "BetterJob", "HowExactly", "MoreInfo", "Responsibility4Choice",
                  "Responsibility4Outcome", "DislikeRelyingOn", "Reactance2Analysis",
                  "PerformanceCuriosity", "Tedious")
res <- t(sapply(items_closed, function(v) {
  tab <- table(factor(delegator_reasons$EVAlgorithm, levels = c(0, 1)),
               factor(delegator_reasons[[v]], levels = c(1, 0)))
  c(Pref = 100 * mean(delegator_reasons[[v]][delegator_reasons$EVAlgorithm == 0] == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    EV   = 100 * mean(delegator_reasons[[v]][delegator_reasons$EVAlgorithm == 1] == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    p    = exact.test(tab, method = "Boschloo", to.plot = FALSE)$p.value)
}))
round(res, 3)
cat("Largest difference (percentage points):", round(max(abs(res[, "Pref"] - res[, "EV"])), 1), "\n")
```

## LPM: never-delegation on reasons

```{r lpm-reasons}
reason_vars <- c("DontTrust", "BetterJob", "HowExactly", "MoreInfo",
                 "Responsibility4Choice", "Responsibility4Outcome",
                 "DislikeRelyingOn", "Reactance2Analysis",
                 "PerformanceCuriosity", "Tedious", "Other")

# Bivariate LPMs (one per reason, HC2 SEs)
bivariate_tbl <- do.call(rbind, lapply(reason_vars, function(rv) {
  m  <- lm(as.formula(paste("as.numeric(sumDeleg0) ~", rv)), data = subjects2)
  ct <- coeftest(m, vcov = vcovHC(m, type = "HC2"))
  data.frame(reason = rv,
             coef = round(ct[2, 1], 3), se = round(ct[2, 2], 3),
             t = round(ct[2, 3], 3), p = round(ct[2, 4], 3))
}))
print(bivariate_tbl, row.names = FALSE)

# Joint LPM: full sample + preference-treatment only
f_joint  <- as.formula(paste("as.numeric(sumDeleg0) ~",
                             paste(reason_vars, collapse = " + ")))
lpm_all  <- lm(f_joint, data = subjects2)
lpm_pref <- lm(f_joint, data = subjects2[subjects2$EVAlgorithm == 0, ])

vcov_all  <- vcovHC(lpm_all,  type = "HC2")
vcov_pref <- vcovHC(lpm_pref, type = "HC2")

screenreg(
  list(lpm_all, lpm_pref),
  override.se = list(sqrt(diag(vcov_all)), sqrt(diag(vcov_pref))),
  override.pvalues = list(
    2 * pt(abs(coef(lpm_all)  / sqrt(diag(vcov_all))),
           df = lpm_all$df.residual,  lower.tail = FALSE),
    2 * pt(abs(coef(lpm_pref) / sqrt(diag(vcov_pref))),
           df = lpm_pref$df.residual, lower.tail = FALSE)
  ),
  custom.model.names = c("Full sample", "Pref. treatment"),
  caption = "LPM: never-delegation ~ reasons (HC2 SEs)"
)
```

# Exclusion-criterion breakdown (Method section)

Reconstructs the exact breakdown of the 7 excluded participants by criterion, as
reported in the Method section (paper: 1 bot/slider failure, 4 careful-participation
failures [`Reliable < 6`], 3 disclosed-AI-usage cases, 0 comprehension-only failures,
0 incomplete-data cases, 0 log-time exclusions; final $N = 233$, with 1 participant
overlapping careful-participation-failure and AI-disclosure). This chunk re-reads the
raw files independently of the exclusions already applied above (using `_raw` suffixes),
so it is self-contained and can be run at any point in the script.

```{r exclusion-breakdown}
choices_raw      <- read.delim("260206_1528_537_lotteryChoices.xls")
prolificData_raw <- read.csv("prolific_demographic_export_approved.csv")

cat("N recruited (Prolific export):", nrow(prolificData_raw), "\n")

choices_raw <- subset(choices_raw, ProlificID %in% prolificData_raw$Participant.id)

part2_raw <- subset(choices_raw, Part == 2)
partvars <- part2_raw[!duplicated(part2_raw$ProlificID),
                       c("ProlificID", "BotCheck1attempt", "Part1CQsPassedOnAttempt",
                         "Part2CQsPassedOnAttempt", "Reliable", "AIUsageInStudy")]

# Incomplete-data flag: participant has zero valid (Delegated >= 0) Part-2 rows
valid_counts <- aggregate(Delegated ~ ProlificID, data = part2_raw,
                           FUN = function(x) sum(x >= 0))
names(valid_counts)[2] <- "nValid"
partvars <- merge(partvars, valid_counts, by = "ProlificID", all.x = TRUE)
partvars$incomplete <- is.na(partvars$nValid) | partvars$nValid == 0

# Log-completion-time "too fast" rule
prolificData_raw$logCompleTime <- log(prolificData_raw$Time.taken)
prolificData_raw$tooFast <- 1 * (
  prolificData_raw$logCompleTime <
    mean(log(prolificData_raw$Time.taken)) - 2 * sd(log(prolificData_raw$Time.taken))
)
partvars <- merge(partvars, prolificData_raw[, c("Participant.id", "tooFast")],
                   by.x = "ProlificID", by.y = "Participant.id", all.x = TRUE)

partvars$failBot      <- partvars$BotCheck1attempt != 1
partvars$failComp     <- partvars$Part1CQsPassedOnAttempt > 2 |
                          partvars$Part2CQsPassedOnAttempt > 2
partvars$failCareful  <- partvars$Reliable < 6
partvars$disclosedAI  <- partvars$AIUsageInStudy != 0

excluded <- subset(
  partvars,
  failBot | failComp | failCareful | disclosedAI | incomplete | tooFast == 1
)

cat("\nTotal excluded:", nrow(excluded), "\n")
cat("Fail bot/slider check:", sum(excluded$failBot), "\n")
cat("Fail comprehension check only:", sum(excluded$failComp), "\n")
cat("Fail careful-participation check (Reliable < 6):", sum(excluded$failCareful), "\n")
cat("Disclosed AI usage:", sum(excluded$disclosedAI), "\n")
cat("Incomplete data:", sum(excluded$incomplete), "\n")
cat("Too fast (log-time rule):", sum(excluded$tooFast == 1, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Overlap (careful-participation AND disclosed AI):",
    sum(excluded$failCareful & excluded$disclosedAI), "\n")
cat("Final analysis N:", nrow(partvars) - nrow(excluded), "\n")
```

# Power analysis (pilot-based, Appendix C of the paper)

Reconstructs the ex-ante power analysis reported in Appendix C (summarized in the Limitations): using
only the pilot's effect sizes (not the present study's own results, to avoid the
retrospective-power fallacy; Hoenig \& Heisey, 2001), we compute the minimum detectable
effect (MDE) at 80% power for $n = 100$--120/arm, and the power to re-detect an effect of
the pilot's observed magnitude. Pilot data: `pilot_data_complete_iw.csv` (an earlier,
non-preregistered study reported in Suraci's PhD thesis).

```{r pilot-data}
pilot <- read.csv("pilot_data_complete_iw.csv")
pilot <- subset(pilot, returned == 1)
cat("Pilot N (returned == 1):", nrow(pilot), "\n")

# EV treatments = 1,2; preference-based (RDU) treatments = 3,4
pilot$EValgo <- 1 * (pilot$treatment %in% c(1, 2))
cat("\nPilot N by condition (0 = Pref, 1 = EV):\n")
print(table(pilot$EValgo))

# First-contact delegation (randomized-order "1st" decision)
cat("\nFirst-contact delegation rate by condition (paper: 45.8% Pref vs. 67.4% EV):\n")
print(aggregate(decision1st ~ EValgo, data = pilot, mean))

# Average delegation across all 8 (randomized-order) decisions
decisioncols <- c("decision1st", "decision2nd", "decision3rd", "decision4th",
                   "decision5th", "decision6th", "decision7th", "decision8th")
pilot$avgDeleg <- rowMeans(pilot[, decisioncols], na.rm = TRUE)
cat("\nAverage delegation rate by condition (paper: 35.3% Pref vs. 54.5% EV):\n")
print(aggregate(avgDeleg ~ EValgo, data = pilot, mean))
```

## Pilot: categorical non-delegation (footnote and Discussion)

The footnote in "Categorical non-delegation" and the Discussion report never-delegation
in the earlier study (paper: 32/189 in preference-based vs. 17/187 in EV treatments,
one-sided Boschloo $p = 0.014$). **Check:** with the pilot data as stored here, the
preference-based arm has 190 participants (as in the first-contact comparison above),
so the denominator should be 190 unless one participant was dropped in the thesis
analysis.

```{r pilot-never-delegators}
pilot$nDeleg <- rowSums(pilot[, decisioncols])
pilotNever <- table(
  Treatment = factor(pilot$EValgo, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Pref", "EV")),
  Never     = factor(pilot$nDeleg == 0, levels = c(TRUE, FALSE),
                     labels = c("Never", "NotNever"))
)
pilotNever
# one-sided Boschloo (Pref > EV), treatment arms as the binomial groups
exact.test(pilotNever, method = "Boschloo", alternative = "greater",
           to.plot = FALSE)$p.value
```

## Minimum detectable effect (MDE) at 80% power

A pure design-stage quantity: depends only on $n$, $\alpha$, and a baseline rate, not on
anything observed in the present study (paper: ~16-17pp for first contact,
~10-11pp for average delegation).

```{r power-mde}
p_pref_firstcontact <- aggregate(decision1st ~ EValgo, data = pilot, mean)[1, 2]

for (n in c(100, 120)) {
  pt <- power.prop.test(n = n, p1 = p_pref_firstcontact, p2 = NULL,
                         power = 0.80, sig.level = 0.05, alternative = "one.sided")
  cat("n =", n, " MDE (first-contact-type proportion) =",
      round(pt$p2 - p_pref_firstcontact, 3), "\n")
}
```

## MDE and power for the average-delegation comparison

Approximated with a one-sided two-sample $t$-test using the pilot's pooled
within-condition SD of participant-average delegation (paper: MDE ~10-11pp;
99.7-99.9% power to re-detect the pilot's ~19pp gap).

```{r power-avgdeleg}
sd_pilot    <- sqrt(mean(tapply(pilot$avgDeleg, pilot$EValgo, var)))
delta_pilot <- diff(tapply(pilot$avgDeleg, pilot$EValgo, mean))
cat("Pilot pooled SD:", round(sd_pilot, 3), " pilot gap:", round(delta_pilot, 3), "\n")

for (n in c(100, 120)) {
  m <- power.t.test(n = n, sd = sd_pilot, power = 0.80, sig.level = 0.05,
                    alternative = "one.sided")
  r <- power.t.test(n = n, delta = delta_pilot, sd = sd_pilot, sig.level = 0.05,
                    alternative = "one.sided")
  cat("n =", n, " MDE =", round(m$delta, 3), " power to re-detect pilot gap =",
      round(r$power, 3), "\n")
}
```

## Power to re-detect the pilot's observed effect

Not a retrospective-power computation on the present study's own effect (which would be
circular); this uses only the pilot's pre-existing effect size as input (paper: 93-96% under the normal approximation, 91-95% by exact-test simulation).

```{r power-redetect}
p_ev_firstcontact <- aggregate(decision1st ~ EValgo, data = pilot, mean)[2, 2]

for (n in c(100, 120)) {
  pt <- power.prop.test(n = n, p1 = p_pref_firstcontact, p2 = p_ev_firstcontact,
                         sig.level = 0.05, alternative = "one.sided")
  cat("n =", n, " power to re-detect pilot's first-contact gap =",
      round(pt$power, 3), "\n")
}
```
